newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, dragged by Egypt, rains.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, dragged by Egypt, rains.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly lower after Egypt bought 600,000 tonnes of non-U.S. wheat at prices that were very competitive with U.S. values, traders said.
Egypt said over the weekend that it bought 200,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, 250,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat and 150,000 tonnes of French wheat.
Traders said wheat also drew pressure from timely rains that fell in HRW wheat regions of the U.S. Central Plains.
But KCBT wheat ended above its intraday lows, thanks to commercially-oriented buying of the December/March spread.
KCBT wheat closed two to eight cents per bushel lower, with December down six cents at $4.20-1/2. March lost eight cents to close at $3.93.

"We did too much, too fast on the upside last week. But the market did do its job of forcing wheat out of the country and now the basis and the inverse are breaking back," a trader said at the midsession. "It just appears that at this time, HRW wheat has priced itself out of the export market."
Traders said E D & F Man International sold one million March bushels. Prudential Securities bought 800,000 Dec and 700,000 March. Term Commodities sold 700,000 March.

Traders said FIMAT bear-spread 1.2 million March/Dec at 25 to 27-1/2 cents. Chicago Corp and FCC each bear-spread one million March/Dec in the same range. Continental bull-spread 700,000 Dec/March at 25 cents.
